title: Batch 47.2 on the 27B (L32; if time, cut first): harder pointer scenes, is the order code ordinal, categorical (first vs rest) or slot-specific? Six-locker routes moves; the slot means fit on a held-out half; removals and writes on the other half (sealed)
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.6-27b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x47_six.py run --name x47_2_27b --why "batch 47, test 47.2 (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml; Q47.2): six-locker routes moves (the bridge's locker sentence moved from slot i to slot j, every ordered pair), the layout-free slot means fit on a held-out half, then on the other half the slot subspace and the old U removed against random parts, pairwise writes mu_t - mu_i, and the shift v = mean_k (mu_k+1 - mu_k) from every start slot; sealed"
question: In six-locker scenes, is the pointer's order code ordinal (a line over slots that one shift vector moves along), categorical (first locker vs the rest), or slot-specific (binding IDs: pairwise moves work, no common shift)?
why_it_matters: The pointer marks the first locker in a clean three-locker layout; the 2nd-vs-3rd removal found no separate direction, yet writing mu_3 - mu_2 moves the lookup at 2x. Three lockers cannot tell "first vs rest" from "a line over slots". Ordinal = a positional line the lens cannot read (Dai et al. 2024's ordering subspace); categorical = a one-bit marker; slot-specific = binding IDs (Feng & Steinhardt 2023).

hypotheses.Q47.2: Dan's answer in predictions/2026-10-28_dan.md (Q47.2: ordinal / categorical, first vs rest / slot-specific, per model: 9B; Muse); not committed when this spec was written, so the run is sealed: no verdict in the job (scripts/x47_six.py verdict refuses until the answer is committed).

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch47.yaml, 47.2): "Ordinal": the first PCA component of the slot means is monotone in slot (|Spearman| >= 0.9) and v sends >= 0.25 of lookups to slot k+1 from >= 4 of 5 start slots, the random vector <= 0.05; "Categorical, first vs rest": v works only from slot 1 (others < 0.10) and U's removal on 2-6 moves is within 0.10 of random; "Slot-specific": pairwise writes reach >= 0.25 on most pairs but no single v does. Dumbest ways: (1) position share near 0 under the whole change -> "not interpretable" (the whole-change routes split reported first); (2) mu_2 - mu_1 reported separately and v fit without it; (3) letters A-H if digits run out. AS COMPUTED (written before any run; Dan may override before the run; scripts/x47_six.py docstring): SCENES: x6_routes' generator (its animal and people pools, sentences, encoding, chat rendering, X0's top-token read) with six single-token animals and their lockers (slots 1-6, six distinct digits of 1-9), the six locker sentences first, then three pick sentences (the asked person picks the bridge, two others pick two other locker items, order seeded), every item's first mention its locker sentence (checked per scene). A routes move (i, j) is x6_routes' C1 at six slots: the bridge's own locker sentence moves from slot i to slot j (swapped with the sentence at slot j; the bridge and the picks stay O's) and the bridge's number in S is a new digit not in O's list (7 of the 9 digits are used: no letters needed). Read on O: identity (= nothing) -> slot i's digit, position -> slot j's digit, value -> the new digit, other. 40 candidates per ordered pair (30 pairs; seed 4702, one stream per pair), the first 20 eligible per pair. C0 sanity (x6_routes' C0 at six slots: S = O with the asked person picking another person's item, the legs differ): 150 candidates, the first 100 eligible, whole change only; its lookup switch reported beside the three-locker reference (x0_massmean_lf_27b), descriptive: it does not stop the run. GATE: X0's competence (8 greedy tokens and the read, unedited O and S, both readers); O's read accuracy >= 0.80 per reader over the 1,200 move candidates; eligible = both readers say and read O's and S's answers right. If six slots miss the gate, the same at five slots (20 pairs x 40 candidates; 4-d slot subspace; (iv) on moves among slots 2-5; the ordinal count needs 4 of 4 start slots), decided by the competence step before any patch and recorded (manifest slots / fallback, gate.json); if five miss too: not tested. SPLIT: per ordered pair, the chosen scenes shuffled (seed 4721 keyed by the pair), the first half (floor) is the fit half, the rest the test half (stratified by pair, not by entity). FIT (in the job, on the fit half, before any arm): O's and S's states at the bridge word at L, each labelled by the bridge's slot in that prompt; x0_massmean's layout-free method (each state minus the mean of its layout group, x0_probe.layout, here the asked pick's place among the three picks; groups of one dropped); mu_k = slot k's mean; the slot subspace W = x0_massmean.mass_mean (orthonormal, rank 5). PCA of the six centred means: the variance explained by 1, 2, 3 components (cumulative), and the Spearman correlation of the first component's projection with slot (computed by the verdict from fit.npz). UNIT: the median over the test half of ||W W^T Delta|| (Delta = h_S - h_O at the bridge word); a write at dose s has norm s x unit. ARMS (test half, on O, at the bridge word at L, both readers): none; whole; (i) Delta - W W^T Delta, and Delta minus a random part of the same share (X0's random subspace, seed 888 + L); (iv) the same for U (the old 4-d basis, x0_massmean.subspaces' Alf on x0_probe_v4_27b, not refit); (ii) from the scene's O slot i to every other slot t, s x unit x (mu_t - mu_i)/||mu_t - mu_i|| (so ~50 scenes per (i, t)); (iii) v = mean_k (mu_k+1 - mu_k) = (mu_6 - mu_1)/5 as s x unit x v/||v|| from start slot i <= 5 (target i + 1), -v from i >= 2 (target i - 1), and for dumbest way 2 mu_2 - mu_1 and v without the first step ((mu_6 - mu_2)/4), each as a shift from i <= 5 (target i + 1); one random unit direction per scene (seed 4723 keyed by the scene) at the same norms, read against every target; s = 1 and 2. RULE as computed: lookup answers classified by the slot whose digit they are; point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9 at the bars), cluster-bootstrap CIs over bridge items (10,000, seed 0) beside them. Decisive dose s = 2 (the motivating write moved the lookup at 2x); every clause also at s = 1, reported beside. "Works" = >= 0.25 of lookups at the target. Ordinal: |Spearman| >= 0.9, v works from >= 4 of the 5 start slots, and the random direction's share at k + 1 pooled over start slots 1-5 <= 0.05. Categorical: v works from slot 1, sends < 0.10 from each of slots 2-5, and on moves with i and j in 2-6 |position share without U - without its random part| <= 0.10. Slot-specific: writes work on most (more than half, >= 16 of 30) ordered pairs and v works from at most 2 of 5 start slots (not most). The first label in this order that holds is the model's answer (all holding labels listed); none: "none of the three". Not interpretable (overrides): the whole change's position share < 0.05. title: Batch 52 B read on Qwen3.5-9B, our main test (X0's scenes): where does the J++ lens read the answer word and the bridge entity? Ranks at the bridge word / earlier mention / question / last token, every second layer, per reader; the plain logit lens's answer layer
command: export BJ_TARGET=qwen3.5-9b BJ_DEVICE_MAP=; uv run python scripts/x52_answer_map.py run --set main --name qwen35_9b_x52_read_main
question: At which token group and layer does the J++ lens have the reader's answer word (and the bridge entity) in its top-5, before the plain logit lens has the answer on top?
why_it_matters: Zach: the answer may be readable straight out of J-space, for both readers. We have pieces (51.12's readout at the bridge word: answer word top-50 on 0.14 / 0.07 / 0.00 of lookup items on our scenes, ~0.53-0.62 on his passages); this makes it one map across token groups and layers, our scenes beside his, and it says where the write test goes.

hypotheses.none: rule fixed in advance in jobs/c3/batch52.yaml (B); no prediction (addendum, Dan 00:25: no Q-lines for batch 52; results opened as they land, UNVERIFIED until hand-checked)

decision_rule: Fixed in advance (jobs/c3/batch52.yaml brief B, Dan 29 Oct 00:30), verbatim: "Rules, fixed in advance. “Readable”: the answer word in the lens top-5 on ≥ 0.5 of items at some layer before the answer layer. “Usable”: writing its directions changes the answer on ≥ 0.3 of items with the random control ≤ 0.10. Report the four combinations per reader, per dataset." No prediction (addendum 00:25): the verdict writes 'rule fixed in advance in jobs/c3/batch52.yaml (B); no prediction'. As computed (fixed before any run): the answer word = 51.12's (scripts/x51_answer.py word_ids: main the number word's one-letter-token variants, 'six' for 6; Z2 the first token of the answer word and its variants), its lens rank = 1 + tokens with a strictly higher J++ readout logit (JLens.readout, full vocabulary; the best variant), on the reader's O prompt; top-5 = rank <= 5; per cell (token group x layer) the share over the items that have that position. Token groups: main B = the bridge word (X0's position), E = the bridge entity's last mention before it (its locker sentence; 100 / 101 / 92 of 200 items have one), Q = the question's 'pick' token (51.10's P2), T = the appended space token (51.10's P3); Z2 B = the description's last token (his edit site), E = the bridge's name in the passage, Q = the question's closing '?', T = the prompt's last token. Layers: every second layer L0 through n_layers - 2 (those in the lens's source layers). The answer layer = per item the first layer at which the plain logit lens (model.unembed of the block output) at T has the answer as read (tok_A) on top; per reader the lower median over items (never: counted, left out); 'before' = cached layers strictly below it; readable if any group has a cell before it with share >= 0.5. Write cell = per reader the cell before the answer layer with the largest top-5 share (ties: lower median rank, earlier layer, B < E < Q < T), point estimates of the read run. Written: u = the unit sum of the unit J++ lens directions (JLens.vectors) of S's answer word's tokens (the answer a real change gives), added at the cell on O at s and 2s, s = ||h_S - h_O|| there (a real change's size; where that is < 1e-3 ||h_O|| because the position comes before O and S differ, the bridge word's ||Δ|| at that layer, flagged). 'Changes the answer' = the top token becomes S's answer's first token (the written answer); 'changed away from O's answer' beside. Usable = at gain 1 or 2, ans_g >= 0.3 with rand_g <= 0.10. Point estimates decide (EPS 1e-9); cluster-bootstrap CIs over the bridge entity (10,000, seed 0) beside. Beside (not in the rules): the bridge entity's ranks (51.12's bridge rank), S's answer word on O (same-type distractor baseline), whole-word variants only (no 'G' for 'Greece', no 'I' for 'Iota'), the digit as read, the plain logit lens's answer-word rank, the frequency-matched write, the whole-state patch at the cell, 51.10's settle layer, and a check against 51.12's readout at the bridge word at X0's L (same items and token sets: top-50 0.14 / 0.07 / 0.00 lookup, 0.28 / 0.12 / 0.01 recall; Z2 9B / 27B ~0.53-0.62).
controls: S's answer word on O at every cell (a same-type distractor: the share any answer of that type reaches)
the answer word's whole-word variants alone (fragments such as 'G' for 'Greece' left out)
the bridge entity's ranks at every cell beside the answer word's (the brief's contrast)
